title: WordPress Backdoor Uses Ethereum Smart Contracts to Hide Command-and-Control Servers
content_md: The malware, found during a site cleanup in mid-June, disguises itself as a legitimate must-use plugin and includes several mechanisms to survive removal. Must-use plugins automatically load on every WordPress request and cannot be disabled through the normal Plugins dashboard . The malware abuses this feature to remain active while hiding from the Must-Use Plugins list, standard plugin pages, update notifications, and Site Health checks. Wordfence released a detection signature on June 23, 2026. Premium, Care, and Response customers received the protection immediately, while free users received it after the standard 30-day delay. Ethereum C2 Backdoor The malware uses custom string obfuscation instead of common base64_decode or eval patterns. It stores important strings in an encoded lookup table and reconstructs WordPress functions, database options, file paths, and hooks only when required. This helps it evade static malware scans and manual analysis. Once installed, the backdoor creates a hidden administrator account or hijacks an existing account by resetting its password. Newly created accounts use names such as admin_xxxxxx , adm_xxxxxx , administrator_xxxxxx , or backup_xxxxxx , followed by six random characters. Real alphabet ($f) (Source: wordfence) It then hides the rogue account from the WordPress Users page and REST API responses .
